sources.entry: More challenging projects every programmer should try: ray tracer, key-value store web API, web browser, stock trading bot.

summary.title: More challenging projects every programmer should try
summary.one_liner: A list of four harder hands-on programming projects (ray tracer, key-value store web API, web browser, stock trading bot) with starting steps and extension ideas for each.
keywords: what happens when you type a url
takeaways: A basic ray tracer can be built in about 300 lines; optimization (threads, profiling, fewer intersection tests) becomes the next challenge.
A key-value store is essentially a dictionary exposed through a web API; extensions include persistence, transactions, and multi-server operation.
A first web browser can be text-only: do an HTTP GET, parse HTML, and print the text, ignoring JavaScript and CSS.
A basic stock trading bot needs a data API, a buy/sell rule, and a paper-money test environment; then backtest and add strategies.
Lowering ray tracer resolution enables real-time animation, an approach the author suggests for indie games.
summary.summary: The author, Austin Henley, extends his earlier list of challenging projects with four more modern ideas. Each project gets a short narrative of what to expect, a suggested starting point, and ideas for going further, such as optimizing a ray tracer, adding persistence and transactions to a key-value store, adding tabs and history to a text browser, or backtesting a trading bot on paper money. Each section ends with a curated further-reading list of tutorials, books, and open-source projects. The post is informal and opinion-driven rather than a step-by-step guide.
